title: Catalog release sync must delete stale JSON assets after upload
answers: deleted model catalog file still downloadable from release
stale model catalog asset remains on model-catalog/latest
how does publish_model_catalog.sh keep release assets in sync
removing a catalog JSON on master does not remove the release asset
body:
Symptom: after a catalog JSON file is removed on master, the old asset is still downloadable from the `model-catalog/latest` release.
Root cause: dev/publish_model_catalog.sh only uploaded files that exist in `$CATALOG_DIR` with `gh release upload --clobber`, and never removed release assets whose source file was gone.
Fix pattern: keep the upload first, then list release assets with `gh release view --json assets` and call `gh release delete-asset` for each `*.json` asset with no matching file in `$CATALOG_DIR`.
Constraints: deletion runs only after a successful upload, so a failed upload cannot remove valid assets. Only `*.json` names are candidates; non-JSON assets are left untouched.
applies: Changes to dev/publish_model_catalog.sh or to how catalog JSON files are added, renamed or removed in mlflow/utils/model_catalog.
says: Deleted model catalog definitions are still available for download from the latest release page.
The public model catalog release contains outdated files that were already removed from source control.
Automatically remove decommissioned model catalog downloads whenever publishing a new release version.
Customers can still download deprecated model catalog entries from the release downloads section.
search: When syncing model catalog releases in dev/publish_model_catalog.sh, stale JSON assets must be deleted from model-catalog/latest after uploading current files. Previously, the script ran gh release upload --clobber for files in $CATALOG_DIR without removing release assets whose source files were deleted. The release sync must list assets via gh release view --json assets and run gh release delete-asset for each *.json asset missing from $CATALOG_DIR. Asset deletion must run only after a successful upload and must strictly target *.json files while leaving non-JSON assets untouched.
